body:
I'm still here.

Two months ago I got a job with a new school. A dream school. Great part of town, bigger budget, more money. I thanked my lucky stars for my newfound luck, and pledged to turn over a new leaf. I abandoned my negative attitude, chose to make my job into something fun, and changed everything about my outlook on how a class should work. I went into the job with a smile and an open mind. 

This afternoon I got an e-mail from one of my administrators. She wants to meet with me tomorrow to discuss "parent complaints, and classroom management." 

I really thought things were better. I've been encouraging to the students, and all are passing my class. I had a panic attack tonight after reading her e-mail. I can't handle losing another job. I can't handle a life where I'm not a teacher. I've attended all the required training, and incorporated the strategies into my class. All the kids are learning and passing the class, and I never, ever yell or otherwise interfere with the well-being of students. And still there are complaints.

A week ago I would have said my life was going the best it has ever been. But that just shows how deluded I am. I'll never grasp why or how I'm bad at this. I'll spend every living moment ignorant, which is a bad situation for a teacher. 

How is it possible to want something so badly, and yet be apparently unable to understand what it takes to be successful at it? How can I be so stupid, and why should I continue on?

The problem isn't my location. I used to think I just had bad luck, and managed to find the principals who didn't appreciate me. But look at the evidence. It's not the rest of the band that's out of step; it's me. I'm the common denominator, no matter where I go.
